what_it_does: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) is an AI model design where a large network is split into many specialized sub-networks called experts; only a few experts are activated for any given input, which keeps computation manageable even as total model size balloons to trillions of parameters. When a model is too large to fit in GPU memory, the experts must be stored on slower CPU memory or disk and loaded on demand. The bottleneck is that loading one expert takes longer than computing with it, so the GPU sits idle waiting. Klotski fixes this by processing multiple batches of inputs at the same time: while the GPU computes on one batch's experts, it loads the experts needed by the next batch. By also routing inputs from different batches that need the same expert together, the compute time grows enough to consistently exceed the load time, eliminating the idle gaps.
